{"text":"{
  "status": "NEEDS_IMPROVEMENT",
  "SYSTEM_INTERPRETATION_OF_USER_INTENT": "The system appears to interpret past interactions as continuing interest in broadly related products or content, with insufficient attention to the specific purpose of the next choice.",
  "WHERE_THE_SYSTEM_GETS_IT_RIGHT": [
    "Recommendations align when they extend a repeated, specific interest, such as storage needs, circuit building, holiday music or melodic metal.",
    "Complementary items appeal when they support an established activity or add a useful capability to equipment users already own."
  ],
  "WHERE_THE_SYSTEM_GETS_IT_WRONG": [
    "Broadly related items compete with stronger matches despite requiring an unrelated project, different listening mood or unestablished equipment need.",
    "Recommendations repeat functions or content users already have without establishing why another version would be useful.",
    "Historical interests appear to outweigh more specific recent patterns, even when older interactions provide uncertain evidence of current intent."
  ],
  "OVERUSED_DECISION_PATTERNS": [
    "Shared category, brand, product line or broad genre appears to substitute for a close match in function or content.",
    "Repeated purchases appear to imply continuing demand for similar items without accounting for needs those purchases may already have satisfied."
  ],
  "UNDERUSED_OR_MISSED_DECISION_PATTERNS": [
    "Specific task, compatibility, dimensions and quantity determine whether a related product is actually usable.",
    "Tone, musical style and the combination of preferred attributes distinguish compelling entertainment choices from broad genre matches.",
    "Recency, repeated narrow interests and added usefulness help distinguish an immediate next choice from something merely plausible.",
    "Unidentified items and ambiguous histories provide weak evidence of preference alignment; feedback about them reflects uncertainty rather than demonstrated dislike."
  ],
  "PRIMARY_FAILURE_MODE_AT_TOP_OF_LIST": "The top recommendations too often establish broad relevance without establishing a specific current reason to choose, allowing duplicates and loosely related items to compete with actionable matches.",
  "DIAGNOSTIC_SIGNALS_TO_TRACK": [
    "The proportion of top-ranked items users would choose now, distinguished from items they consider relevant but would defer.",
    "The frequency of top-ranked rejections attributed to unrelated purpose, incompatible specifications, excessive quantity or duplicated functionality.",
    "The relative ranks of items matching repeated specific interests versus items connected only by broad category, brand or genre.",
    "The proportion of recommendation judgments that remain uncertain because item identity or historical preference evidence is insufficient."
  ]
}"}
